edition.locus: Abdomia, Libyan phriton, and the Roman apple

source_text:
Τῶν
καλουμένων «ἀβδωμίων» ξέστας δέκα καὶ στάγματος Λιβυκοῦ Λιβύης τῆς
εὐδαίμονος (ὃ δὴ «φρίτον» οἱ ἐπιχώριοι καλοῦσι) τοσοῦτον ὑσσώπου τε Κρητικοῦ
δέσμην καὶ μῆλον τὸ Ῥωμαϊκὸν («ὀρβικλάτον» δὲ καλούμενον) ἅμα μέλιτος
κοτύλαις ἑκκαίδεκα κιρνῶν, ἕψει <σὺν> συκίνῳ κλάδῳ ἐφ' ἡμέρας τρεῖς ἠδ' ὥραις
τρισὶ καθ' ἑκάστην ἡμέραν μαλακῷ πυρί, κἀκεῖνος ἀποβήσεται.
pass_a_gloss: Of the called 'abdomia' xestai ten and of-stagmas Libyan of-Libya the fortunate (which 'phriton' the locals call) so-much and of-hyssop Cretan a bundle and apple the Roman ('orbiclatum' being-called) together of-honey cotylai sixteen mixing, boil with a fig-branch upon days three and hours three according-to each day with-soft fire, and that too will-turn-out.
pass_b_english: Of the so-called abdomia, ten xestai, and as much Libyan stagmas of fortunate Libya (which the locals call phriton), and a bundle of Cretan hyssop, and the Roman apple (called orbiclatum), mixing them with sixteen cotylai of honey, boil with a fig branch for three days and three hours each day on a gentle fire, and that too will turn out.

choices.english: and that too will turn out
choices.why: Continues the previous farming recipes: this mixture also 'comes out' as the desired product.

anf_compare.notes: No PD English of the Cesti body; ANF has the letters only.
